items.title: (1 of 2) French Walnut Armchair
items.description:
One of two walnut armchairs. The set are constructed of sturdy wood and feature draping foliage carved into the arms both at the front of the chair and where the arm connects to the backing. The legs are turned wood, and the feet are carved to sit with wide unfurling curves akin to a flower turned up-side-down. The flowers themselves vary in style with some appearing like peonies, others like daffodils and others as tulips or hydrangeas. The bulk of the florals are pink and white, though some feature blue  instead.
This chair is positioned on the right side of the couch.

items.title: (1 of 4) Floral and Scallop Shell Carved Armchair
items.description:
An English Style armchair carved extensively with details along most of the wooden surfaces. The back is the most intricate piece with the seat back carved with scallop shells and arabesque leaves ornamenting the borders. An 18-pettled flower with a wide center akin to samplers are carved into the center of the top rail, and four-petaled flowers are depicted at each corner, bordered by more arabesques. The ears, legs and lower crossrail are all turned into the shape of a spiral, with joining blocks carved with flowers with full round petals. The tops and sides are the arm rests are coved, though in lower relief and detail, with a simplified version of the arabesques on the seat back. The wooden sides of the seat match with flowers at the center of each cross-rail. The seat and the center of the backrest are upholstered in a red fabric that is not patterned but has some level of texture to it.
Part of a set of 4 chairs - two are in the living room, one is in the library, one is in the basement. This one is on the right side of the table in the living room.

items.title: Tapestry with Unicorns
items.description:
A large tapestry woven in golds and reds. The center image depicts two unicorns, facing each other where they both raise up on their rears legs. They stand on either side of an oval medallion, within which are three Fleur de lis. Fabric coils into a roll beneath the medallion, and the fabric is then depicted rising over the medallion and the unicorns draped like the entrance to a tent. Above the medallion and shielded by this drapery is an open crown. At the top of the image a second crown, this one closed with a cap of red fabric, seems to hold the rest of the center imagery aloft. Around the edges architectural arabesques are rendered to appear hollow; the are interspersed with small florals, creating a border around the center image.
This tapestry is paired with a much smaller tapestry, almost half the size, and hung from the long end instead of the short. They depict identical imagery. Both Tapestries are of Modern Construction. Though some elements are highly reminiscent of historic crests - most notably the dual unicorns of the Scottish Coat Of Arms, - the crest depicted does not seem to represent a specific coat of arms from history.

items.title: Five Paintings of the Life of Christ
items.description:
Five Scenes from the life of Christ. The set appears to have gone together originally, but the frame to display them together is a modern commission specifically designed to house them.
The first scene is the Annunciation of the Virgin Mary (From Luke 1). The Virgin is depicted sitting to the right side of the image. At the left, an Angel, (Gabriel) approaches her, and a dove is suspended the air above them both, symbolizing the holy spirit. This is a common composition for the iconography.
The second image depicts a Young Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2). In this scene his parents find the young man surrounded by teachers from the temple, where he has been learning for 3 days. All those who observed the scene were amazed by his understanding.
The third scene shows an adult Jesus standing among his sleeping apostles. An Angel is presenting a vision, probably the one he has in Luke 9 of his covenant and death. The angel holds a cross and a chalice.
The fourth scene depicts the torture of Jesus Christ at the hands of Pontius Pilot and his men. This is from Mark 15 and precedes his crucifixion. Two men whip his back as he stands looking forlorn with his arms tied behind his back.
The final scene shows Christ carrying the cross (John 19). Two men walk in front of him, one with a horn, heralding the procession. A fourth man stands over his left shoulder and assists him carrying the cross. This is likely Simon of Cyrene, who carries the cross for a portion of the procession.

items.title: White Marble Pedestal
items.description:
A carved White Marble Pedestal, which supports the statue of Suzanna in the back yard. The Pedestal itself is carved with scenes depicting her story.
Also called Suzanna and the elders, the story is told of a beautiful young woman. In the privacy of her walled garden, Suzanna bathes, but is spied by two elders of the village, both of whom covet her. Working together they try to bribe her into having sex, threatening to say she has committed adultery if she refuses. When she refuses, the elders hold to the threat and make a public accusation of adultery. It is only after the two men are cross-examined by Daniel and reveal discrepancies in their stories that Suzanna is proven innocent.
Suzanna's story is only considered to be canonical in the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Oriental Orthodox churches.In these denominations the story is part of the book of Daniel. In most other denominations of Christianity, Suzanna's story is not considered cannon, but it is considered to be useful for teaching. The motif of the story is very common in artwork. Images depicting the tale date back to as early as the 9th century. It was particularly popular in the 15th and 16th centuries. When painted the image usually depicts Suzanna and the two voyeurs in a scene. When sculpted in the round, Suzanna is usually depicted alone.
In the context of Krebs House, the Suzanna statue (KR23.2.27) sits atop the White Marble Pedestal (KR23.3.10), framed by a Italian Stone Rotunda (KR23.3.11), and set as the focal point of a fountain.

items.title: 19th Century Marble Column Pedestal
items.description:
An elaborately carved white marble pillar, standing more than 5 feet tall. On the pillar, sections are carved. The base is curled to present as large leaves. Above that the lowest section of the pillar is carved to show birds and foliage. Above that a narrow band shows grape vines and leaves are carved to stand in the round out from the pillar. Another section is carved to show narrower leaves, akin to those at the base. This is followed by a larger section at the top, at the base of which four male heads are carved. Each face is the same, with long curly hair and a full mustache and beard. Branches of a fruiting tree with fanning leaves (maybe olives?) are sculpted into the rest of the section above their heads. Then the capital.
The pillar supports an Italian Terracotta Bust of a woman (entered separately as KR23.2.8a).
